segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Again he began to teach beside the sea. A very large crowd gathered around him, so that he got into a boat and sat in it out on the sea, while the whole crowd was on the land, facing the sea.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He taught them many things in parables, and in his teaching he said to them:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Listen! Look, a sower went out to sow.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And as he sowed, some seed fell along the path, and the birds came and ate it up.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Other seed fell on the rocky ground, where it did not have much soil, and it sprang up at once because it had no depth of soil.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And when the sun rose it was scorched, and because it had no root it withered.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Other seed fell among the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it gave no crop.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Other seeds fell into the good soil and gave a crop, coming up and growing, and bore thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he was alone, those around him, together with the Twelve, asked him about the parables.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “To you has been given the secret of the kingdom of God; but to those outside, everything comes in parables,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: so that they may look and look but not see, and hear and hear but not understand; otherwise they might turn back and be forgiven.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You do not know what this parable means? Then how will you understand all the parables?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The sower sows the word.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: These are the ones along the path, where the word is sown: when they hear, Satan comes at once and takes away the word that has been sown in them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And likewise these are the ones sown on the rocky ground: when they hear the word, they at once receive it with joy,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: yet they have no root in themselves and last only for a time; then, when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, at once they fall away.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And others are the ones sown among the thorns: these are the ones who have heard the word,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: but the worries of the age, the deceitfulness of wealth, and desires for everything else come in and choke the word, and it yields no crop.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And those are the ones sown on the good soil: they hear the word and welcome it and bear a crop, thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Does the lamp come to be put under the measuring bowl or under the bed? Is it not to be put on the lampstand?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For nothing is hidden except to be brought to light, and nothing has been concealed except to come to light.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If anyone has ears to hear, let them hear.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Pay attention to what you hear. With the measure you measure by, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever has will be given more; and whoever does not have, even what they have will be taken away from them.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The kingdom of God is like this: it is as if someone were to scatter seed on the ground

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and sleep and rise, night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows tall, though he does not know how.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: On its own the earth bears a crop: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But when the crop is ripe, at once he sends in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “To what shall we compare the kingdom of God, or what parable shall we use for it?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: It is like a mustard seed, which, when it is sown on the ground, is smaller than all the seeds on the earth—

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: yet when it is sown, it comes up and becomes larger than all the garden plants and puts out large branches, so that the birds of the sky can nest in its shade.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as far as they were able to hear;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: he did not speak to them without a parable, but in private he explained everything to his own disciples.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Let us cross over to the other side.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Leaving the crowd, they took him with them in the boat, just as he was; and other boats were with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a great windstorm arose, and the waves were breaking into the boat, so that the boat was already filling.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he was in the stern, asleep on the cushion. They woke him and said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He woke up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Quiet! Be silent!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the wind dropped, and there was a great calm.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why are you such cowards? Do you still not have faith?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they were filled with great fear and said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

notes.note: This is the Sea of Galilee, a freshwater lake about thirteen miles long. Mark calls it a 'sea', following Semitic usage in which one word covers both lakes and seas; Luke calls it a 'lake'. 'Sea' is kept because the word matters at the end of the chapter, where the wind and the sea obey Jesus in language that recalls Old Testament descriptions of God ruling the sea.

notes.traditional: some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some a hundred
notes.note: The manuscripts differ over a small word repeated before each number, which can be read as 'one' or as 'in' (or 'up to'); early copies had no accents to distinguish them. The reading 'one thirty, one sixty, one a hundred' probably reflects an Aramaic way of saying 'thirtyfold'. The sense is hardly affected.

Older translations have 'mystery', which in modern English suggests a puzzle or something unknowable. In Jewish Greek of the period the word meant a secret, especially a divine plan hidden until God discloses it. Many modern versions also use 'secret'.

The wording adapts Isaiah 6:9–10, in a form close to the Aramaic paraphrase used in synagogues ('be forgiven' rather than 'be healed'). The Greek most naturally expresses purpose, and is translated that way. Many interpreters soften it to result ('with the result that') or take it as shorthand for 'so that Scripture is fulfilled'. The final clause can also be read as 'unless perhaps they turn back'. The question is much disputed.

The Greek word denotes a period of time, here the present age as distinct from the age to come, rather than the world as a place. Most translations have 'world', and the practical meaning is similar. 'Age' keeps the contrast of two eras that a first-century Jewish hearer would have recognised.

The Greek literally says that the lamp 'comes', an odd verb for a household object, and most translations smooth it to 'is brought'. Some interpreters think the wording hints that the lamp stands for Jesus or his message, which has 'come'. Others take it as a Semitic idiom meaning no more than 'is brought'. The literal wording is kept so that readers can judge for themselves.

The word is a Latin loanword for a standard dry-measure container holding a little under nine litres, found in most households. 'Bushel' in older versions names a much larger English measure and is now unfamiliar to many readers.

The wording echoes Joel 3:13, 'Send in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe', where harvest is an image of God's final judgment. A hearer who knew the prophets would have caught the allusion to the end of the age.

notes.traditional: the birds of the air / the fowls of heaven
notes.note: The Greek word covers both 'heaven' and the visible sky, and the sky is meant here. The picture of birds sheltering in the branches recalls Old Testament images of a great tree that stands for a kingdom giving shelter to the nations (Ezekiel 17:23; 31:6; Daniel 4:12).

The two commands mean 'be quiet' and, literally, 'be muzzled', that is, be silenced and stay silent. 'Rebuked' and the second command are the same words Mark uses when Jesus silences an unclean spirit in 1:25. The traditional 'Peace! Be still!' hides that link and sounds gentler than the Greek.

The Greek adjective means cowardly or timid and was a term of reproach, different from the ordinary word for fear used in the next verse. Most translations render both as 'afraid', which blurs the contrast between the disciples' cowardice in the storm and their awe afterwards. Some manuscripts read 'How is it that you have no faith?' in the second question.
